title: Wavelength of an electron against accelerating voltage
caption: Accelerated through V an electron has λ = h/√(2meV) ≈ 1.23/√V nm. At 100 V that is 0.12 nm, comparable with atomic spacings, which is why electrons diffract from crystals; at the lesson's 150 V it is 0.10 nm. Raising the voltage by 4 only halves the wavelength.
alt: Graph of electron wavelength in nanometres against accelerating voltage from 20 to 400 volts: a falling curve through 0.12 at 100 volts and 0.10 at 150 volts.
description: The horizontal axis is the accelerating voltage V in volts; the vertical axis is the electron's de Broglie wavelength in nanometres.
The curve is λ = 1.23/√V nm, from λ = h/√(2meV).
A larger voltage gives a shorter wavelength, falling as 1/√V.
